answer: Peers verify stake provenance like mapping every inlet feeding a meadow, tracing deposits to distinct origins. Each agent stakes a bond locked to a unique hardware-attested identity; forging extra identities means posting fresh collateral per pseudonym, so a sybil fleet becomes a costly voyage through duplicated stakes that the attacker cannot recover if slashed. Duplicate roots get rejected, forcing attackers to burn capital per fake node while honest participants pay once. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
